run.notes: First light for the rig and for the `local` platform slot. Two tools: llama-bench for the single-stream configuration sweep (concurrency 1 by construction), and llama-batched-bench for the concurrency sweep. A FORCE_MMQ rebuild was also tested and rejected.

hardware.accelerator: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 Ti with Max-Q Design

host.notes: TU117, compute capability 7.5, NO tensor cores. 12 CPU cores. Driver 610.57.04, CUDA 13.3. Not comparable to the T4-based g4dn/g5g rigs despite the matching compute capability: the T4 is TU104 and has tensor cores.

model.architecture_notes: llama.cpp reports 4.63 B params / 3.10 GiB. Slot-5 `q4_0` is what MODEL_NAME calls the export; by bytes the file is 67.7% Q6_K and 31.4% Q4_0. per_layer_token_embd (1.927 GB, 58% of the file) is TENSOR_READ_LAZY and never becomes resident.

memory.notes: MEASURED 1618 MiB total via nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps, against 1616 MiB predicted. usable_hbm_gib is the 3725 MiB llama.cpp reports, not the 4096 MiB nameplate. weights_gib EXCLUDES per_layer_token_embd (1.927 GB) because TENSOR_READ_LAZY keeps it host-side in the mmap; sizing from the 3.35 GB file would predict a model that cannot load on this card, and it loads with 2.1 GiB spare. A second configuration was measured for the batched case: -c 16384 --parallel 16 occupies 1818 MiB, leaving 1903 MiB free.

workload.notes: llama-bench reports prefill (pp512) and decode (tg128) as separate tests. output_tok_per_s below is tg128; the pp512 figure for the same configuration is in each point's raw block.

issues.summary: llama.cpp warns at init that this device lacks tensor cores and suggests CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=61-virtual;80-virtual plus GGML_CUDA_FORCE_MMQ. TESTED: a FORCE_MMQ build at arch=75 measured pp512 337.61 / tg128 73.04 against the stock build's 340.33 / 73.75 — a wash, marginally worse. The 61-virtual;80-virtual half of the suggestion was not tested; decode is not matmul-bound here, so it is unlikely to pay.

The -ctk/-ctv q8_0 sweep was cut short by a 2-minute command timeout: the q8_0/q8_0 combination and the t=6/t=8 rows of the q8_0 configurations were not run. Not pursued because both single-sided q8_0 configurations were already clear regressions.

Max-Q thermal variance is real and large enough to invert a curve. A first concurrency sweep measured B=32 at 184.09 tok/s, BELOW B=16's 238.41; a re-run of the same command measured 258.28 and restored monotonicity. Do not read a single batched-bench row as a result.

notes: Nothing here is a serving benchmark: llama-bench drives the model directly, with no HTTP path and no concurrency. Every sweep point is concurrency 1 by construction, not by measurement.
The rig's llama-server was verified healthy separately, and is what the 1618 MiB memory figure was measured against — not llama-bench.

KV cache quantization is a LOSS on this card: q8_0 on either K or V costs ~12% of decode and 20-40% of prefill. There are no tensor cores and the KV is only ~144 MiB, so the dequant work buys memory that is not scarce.
Thread count is irrelevant (73.75 / 73.08 / 72.97 at t=4/6/8) — decode is GPU-bound.
Do not compare these numbers against the T4-based g4dn/g5g rigs on the strength of a shared compute capability 7.5: the T4 is TU104 and has tensor cores, TU117 has none.

Batching is the largest lever on this card by far: aggregate decode goes 73.33 (B=1) -> 223.75 (B=8) -> 277.61 (B=64), a 3.8x. Per-stream falls correspondingly (73.33 -> 4.3), so pick the point from whether the workload is one interactive session or many.
Prefill is flat at ~355 t/s across every concurrency from 1 to 64, so the prefill path is already saturated at B=1 and batching buys nothing there.

Gemma 4 reasons. llama.cpp routes the thinking block to `reasoning_content` and leaves `content` empty until it closes: at max_tokens=64 the reply is finish_reason 'length' with EMPTY content; at 400 it is 'TPU v1, TPU v2, TPU v5' after 1274 chars of reasoning. Every -n 128 figure in this report therefore measures the thinking phase, which is fine for tok/s and misleading as a task.
